title: File-descriptor leak on an error path exhausts the connection limit
source_note: Failure pattern (connections not closed on a specific error path, so file descriptors leak until the process hits 'too many open files' and cannot accept or open new connections) is a standard resource-exhaustion class in the Google SRE Book. All services, log lines, metrics, and timestamps are fabricated for evaluation.
incident_report: Since ~08:30 UTC proxy-service is returning 5xx on about a third of requests and the rate is climbing. No deploys today. inventory-api had a spell of errors earlier this morning.

signal_lines.msg: open file descriptors 38000 / 40000 limit and climbing
fd count not dropping during low traffic; connections to inventory-api not being released
accept() failing: too many open files (EMFILE)
cannot open new upstream connections; 5xx rate 30%
operator restarted proxy-service pods; fd count reset; leak on the inventory-api error path still open

ground_truth.root_cause: proxy-service leaks file descriptors on one error path: connections opened to inventory-api during a request are not closed when that request hits a specific downstream error, so the socket and its fd stay open indefinitely. An earlier spell of inventory-api errors accelerated the leak; open fds climbed from ~8k toward the 40k limit. Once the limit was hit, proxy-service could not accept new connections or open upstream ones ('too many open files'), so ~30% of requests failed. A restart resets the fd count but the leak remains until the error-path code is fixed.
evidence_path: proxy-service open fds climb steadily toward the 40k limit and do not drop even during low traffic - a leak, not load
the fd growth is tied to un-released connections to inventory-api on an error path
proxy-service ERROR: accept() failing with 'too many open files' (EMFILE)
error_rate rises to ~30% once new connections cannot be opened
restarting the pods resets fds but does not fix the leak
ground_truth.fix: Restart affected pods to restore service (done). Fix the inventory-api client to close the connection in a finally block on every path including errors, add an open-fd-count alert, and add a leak test that exercises the error path.
